Flash
Design
System

Built for designers and engineers, the Flash Design System provides the foundations, components and guidance needed to create fast, accessible and recognisably Flash interfaces.

A unified system of principles, components and patterns for building consistent Flash experiences across products and platforms.

Foundations
Colour, typography, iconography and layout foundations that define the Flash visual language.
Components
Reusable building blocks designed for consistency, scalability and implementation across products.

Brand essence

Clarity
Interfaces should communicate hierarchy and intent immediately.
Aa
Confidence
Use strong typography, deliberate spacing and clear actions.
Energy
Use Flash Green intentionally to create emphasis and momentum.

Foundations

Colour Tokens

Primitives define the raw scale — semantics map them to named roles. Hover any swatch to inspect; click to copy.

Core colours
The Flash palette is built on three colours. Green is the brand, but it's emphasis — not a default. Black and white do most of the work; green marks the single most important thing.
Flash Green
#1DFA0F
Primary — emphasis, CTAs, the spark
Black
#000000
Primary text, dark surfaces
White
#FFFFFF
Text on dark, light surfaces
Mid Green
#10C504
Forest Green
#003F1E
Medium Green
#3FB549
Light Grey
#F0F0F0
Green is emphasis, not decoration. Aim for one green moment per screen. On light surfaces, use Mid Green #10C504 for accents — never Flash Green as text on white.

' fam__col--base' : '';\n    const isOpacity = sw.h.startsWith('rgba');\n    const blockStyle = isOpacity\n      ? `background:${sw.bg||'#ffffff'}`\n      : `background:${sw.h}`;\n    const overlay = isOpacity\n      ? `<div style=\"position:absolute;inset:0;background:${sw.h}\"></div>`\n      : '';\n    const displayVal = fmtColor(sw.h);\n    return `<div class=\"fam__col${baseClass}\" onclick=\"copy('${sw.h}','${fam.name} ${sw.s}')\">\n      <div class=\"fam__block\" style=\"${blockStyle}\">\n        ${overlay}\n        <div class=\"fam__tip\">${fam.name} ${sw.s}<br>${displayVal}</div>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"fam__meta\">\n        <div class=\"fam__step\">${sw.s}</div>\n        <div class=\"fam__hex\">${displayVal}</div>\n      </div>\n    </div>`;\n  }).join('');\n\n  el.innerHTML = `\n    <div class=\"fam__head\">\n      <div class=\"fam__info\">\n        <div class=\"fam__name\">${fam.name}</div>\n        <div class=\"fam__desc\">${fam.desc}</div>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"fam__badge fam__badge--${fam.badgeCls}\">${fam.badge}</div>\n    </div>\n    ${hasBase ? '<div class=\"fam__legend\"><span class=\"fam__legend-dot\"></span> = base step</div>' : ''}\n    <div class=\"fam__strip\">${strip}</div>`;\n  return el;\n}\n\nfunction getSemHex(fl,fd,vl,vd) {\n  // Flash brand only; light/dark follows the global theme.\n  return currentTheme()==='dark' ? fd : fl;\n}\n\nfunction renderSemGroup(key) {\n  const group = SEM[key];\n  const panel = document.getElementById('sem-'+key);\n  if (!panel) return;\n\n  const rows = group.rows.map(([v,fl,fd,vl,vd,note]) => {\n    const hex = getSemHex(fl,fd,vl,vd);\n    const prim = HEX_PRIM[hex] || '';\n    const name = v.replace(/^--/,'');\n    return `<tr>\n      <td><span class=\"sem-var\" onclick=\"copy('var(${v})','CSS var')\">${name}</span></td>\n      <td>\n        <div class=\"sem-color-cell\">\n          <div class=\"sem-swatch\" style=\"background:${hex}\"></div>\n          <div class=\"sem-color-meta\">\n            <span class=\"sem-hex\">${hex}</span>\n            ${prim ? `<span class=\"sem-prim\">${prim}</span>` : ''}\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      </td>\n      <td class=\"sem-note\">${note}</td>\n    </tr>`;\n  }).join('');\n\n  panel.innerHTML = `\n    <div class=\"sem-group-block\">\n      <div class=\"sem-group-title\">${group.title}</div>\n      <table class=\"sem-table\">\n        <thead><tr>\n          <th>Token</th>\n          <th>Colour · Primitive</th>\n          <th>Usage</th>\n        </tr></thead>\n        <tbody>${rows}</tbody>\n      </table>\n    </div>`;\n}\n\nfunction refreshSem() {\n  Object.keys(SEM).forEach(renderSemGroup);\n}",

Typography

Satoshi Variable across both brands. One shared type scale — primitive weight tokens (Medium 500 · Semibold 650 · Bold 800 · Black 900) used as source of truth. Desktop and Mobile heading sets defined separately.

Typography
Two typefaces, clearly divided. Never swap their roles.
Aa
Satoshi
The workhorse. All app UI, body copy, labels, and most headlines. A variable font spanning Light to Black.
AA
Kilimanjaro Sans
Display only. Short, punchy marketing headlines — loud, wide, uppercase. Never body copy.

Foundations

Icons v1.2.0

Font Awesome Solid & Outline icons, vendored as inline SVG — no icon font, no build step, no external requests. Every icon is fully customisable with plain CSS: set color to recolour, and the --icn-size custom property (or width/height) to resize. Icons by Font Awesome, used under CC BY 4.0.

Style
Solid is the default weight and covers every icon. Outline is available for a subset — icons without an Outline twin fall back to Solid and are hidden from the Library below while Outline is selected. Pick one style per view; don’t mix Solid and Outline in the same list, toolbar, or screen.
Customise size & colour
Drag the slider to resize, tap a swatch to recolour. Both are just CSS — --icn-size and color — set directly on the .icn wrapper.
Size 40px
Colour
Sizes
Four steps cover most contexts — inline text, buttons, list rows and standalone use. Follows the Style toggle above.
Small · 16
Regular · 24
Large · 32
XL · 48
Library
64 icons for common actions and objects — used throughout this design system, including the Navigation section below. Click a tile to copy its name.
Anatomy & specs
Every icon is a single filled shape (Solid) or its lighter-weight Outline twin where one exists — never a stroke-based glyph, so any icon can substitute for another within the same style without a visual seam.
PropertyValue
SourceFont Awesome 6 Solid & Outline (Regular), vendored as inline SVG
FillcurrentColor, no stroke — true for both Solid and Outline
GridPer-icon viewBox (Font Awesome's native proportions)
ColourcurrentColor — set color on .icn
Size--icn-size custom property (default 24px)
Markup<span class="icn"><svg>…</svg></span>
When to use
Icons speed up scanning when they’re unambiguous. When in doubt, pair one with a text label.
✓ Do
  • Default to Solid for filled, high-emphasis icons; reach for Outline for a lighter, secondary emphasis (e.g. an unselected nav or tab state).
  • Pick one style — Solid or Outline — per view, and keep every icon in it consistent.
  • Recolour and resize with color and --icn-size, not by editing the SVG.
  • Label icon-only buttons with aria-label or a tooltip.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t mix Solid and Outline within the same list, toolbar, or screen — pick one and stay consistent.
  • Don’t assume every icon has an Outline twin — check the Library tile before switching a whole view; icons without one silently render Solid.
  • Don’t use an icon alone for a critical, unfamiliar action.
  • Don’t hardcode a fill colour on an icon — it breaks dark mode.

    "do": [
      "Default to Solid for filled, high-emphasis icons; reach for Outline for a lighter, secondary emphasis (e.g. an unselected nav or tab state).",
      "Pick one style — Solid or Outline — per view, and keep every icon in it consistent.",
      "Recolour and resize with color and --icn-size, not by editing the SVG.",
      "Label icon-only buttons with aria-label or a tooltip."
    ],
    "dont": [
      "Don’t mix Solid and Outline within the same list, toolbar, or screen — pick one and stay consistent.",
      "Don’t assume every icon has an Outline twin — check the Library tile before switching a whole view; icons without one silently render Solid.",
      "Don’t use an icon alone for a critical, unfamiliar action.",
      "Don’t hardcode a fill colour on an icon — it breaks dark mode."
    ]

The real function (near ICONS/renderIcons) is a 3-line helper: looks up ICONS[name] (falling back to ICONS.info) and wraps its viewBox/path data in an <svg fill=\"currentColor\" aria-hidden=\"true\">."

Brand

Logos

The Flash mark and wordmark, in the four supported colour treatments — each as a horizontal lockup and a stacked lockup. Every tile is downloadable as SVG or PNG.

The logo
A bull silhouette in a green circle, paired with the lowercase flash wordmark. The variant changes with the background so the mark always has contrast.
On black
On Flash Green — black mark
On white — green icon
Never recreate the logo. Always use the supplied SVG files, keep clear space around it, and use one logo per layout.
Primary
Green mark, black wordmark. Default lockup for light backgrounds.
Horizontal
Mark and wordmark side by side.
SVG PNG
Stacked
Mark above wordmark, for tighter or square spaces.
SVG PNG
White
Green mark, white wordmark. For dark or brand-coloured backgrounds.
Horizontal
Mark and wordmark side by side.
SVG PNG
Stacked
Mark above wordmark, for tighter or square spaces.
SVG PNG
Monochrome — Black
Single-colour black, for contexts where the brand green can't be reproduced.
Horizontal
Mark and wordmark side by side.
SVG PNG
Stacked
Mark above wordmark, for tighter or square spaces.
SVG PNG
Monochrome — White
Single-colour white, for dark or photographic backgrounds where colour can't be reproduced.
Horizontal
Mark and wordmark side by side.
SVG PNG
Stacked
Mark above wordmark, for tighter or square spaces.
SVG PNG
Usage
The mark and wordmark are fixed assets — treat them as a single unit, not raw material to restyle.
✓ Do
  • Pick the variant (Primary, White, Monochrome Black/White) that gives the strongest contrast against its background.
  • Keep clear space around the logo — at least the height of the bull mark on every side.
  • Use the stacked lockup when horizontal space is tight or the container is square; use horizontal everywhere else.
  • Scale the logo proportionally using the SVG whenever possible for crisp rendering at any size.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t place the logo over busy photography, patterned, or low-contrast backgrounds.
  • Don’t recolour, gradient-fill, or apply drop shadows, outlines, or other effects to the mark or wordmark.
  • Don’t stretch, skew, rotate, or otherwise distort the logo’s proportions.
  • Don’t redraw, crop, or separate the bull mark from the wordmark outside of the provided lockups.
  • Don’t place the logo tighter than its minimum clear space, or shrink it below a legible size.

Buttons v1.5.4

5 variants · 5 sizes · 5 states · light & dark mode. Use the playground to interact with any combination, then expand variants below to see the full reference grid.

Hierarchy & when to use which
Variants are ordered by emphasis: Primary → Secondary → Accent → Simple → Link. Reach for Primary and Secondary first — Accent is a spotlight, not a default.
✓ Do
  • Use Primary for the main action on a screen — there should usually be only one per view.
  • Use Secondary for supporting actions alongside a Primary button.
  • Reserve Accent for the one or two moments per page that genuinely need extreme contrast and visual highlighting — a hero CTA, a rare high-value promo.
  • Use Simple and Link for low-emphasis or inline actions where a filled button would compete with more important content.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t default to Accent — if every button is a spotlight, nothing is.
  • Don’t use more than one or two Accent buttons on the same page outside of a deliberate, high-contrast exception.
  • Don’t place two Primary buttons side by side — pair Primary with Secondary or Simple instead.

Text Inputs v2.1.0

Unified Trader input system — Standard (floating/inline label) and Search (pill) families · 2 sizes · every state, background context and icon slot · state-journey map and icon reference sheet below.

Hierarchy & when to use which
Two families: Standard for entering or editing a value, Search for filtering/finding within a set of results. Don’t reach for one to do the other’s job.
✓ Do
  • Use the Standard field for any value the user types and submits — names, amounts, references, passwords.
  • Default to Caption label mode (the label floats above the value) so the field’s purpose stays visible once it’s filled in; reach for Inline only in tight, compact layouts where a persistent floated label would crowd the row.
  • Use the Search pill only for filtering/finding within a results set, and pair it with a real loading state while results are being fetched.
  • Show helper text for format guidance (e.g. expected pattern) and switch to the error state with a concrete, specific message when validation actually fails.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use the Search pill as a general-purpose text field — its shape and icon promise filtering, not data entry.
  • Don’t rely on placeholder text as the only label — every field keeps a real, persistent label so the value’s meaning is never lost once it’s filled in.
  • Don’t show the error state without a specific, actionable message — a red border with no explanation just tells the user something’s wrong, not what to fix.
  • Don’t add a leading or trailing icon purely for decoration — every icon slot should communicate something (an action, a field type, a state).

TI_ICONS[tiState.leading][tiState.size] : null;\n  const trailingSvg = (tiState.trailingEnabled && tiState.trailing!=='none') ? TI_ICONS[tiState.trailing][tiState.size] : null;\n  const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n  wrap.innerHTML = `\n    <div class=\"ti-shell\" data-bg=\"${tiState.bg}\" data-size=\"${tiState.size}\">\n      <div class=\"ti-field\" data-bg=\"${tiState.bg}\" data-size=\"${tiState.size}\">\n        ${leadingSvg ? `<span class=\"ti-leading\">${leadingSvg}</span>` : ''}\n        <span class=\"ti-label\">Label</span>\n        <div class=\"ti-value-row\">\n          ${tiState.password ? '<div class=\"ti-dots\"></div>' : `<input class=\"ti-input\" type=\"text\" autocomplete=\"off\" spellcheck=\"false\"/>`}\n          <span class=\"ti-mirror\"></span>\n          <span class=\"ti-caret\"></span>\n        </div>\n        <div class=\"ti-trailing\">\n          ${trailingSvg ? `<span class=\"ti-trailing-icon\">${trailingSvg}</span>` : ''}\n          <button class=\"ti-eye\" type=\"button\" aria-label=\"Toggle password visibility\">${TI_EYE_SHOW_SVG}</button>\n          <button class=\"ti-clear\" type=\"button\" aria-label=\"Clear\">${TI_CLEAR_SVG}</button>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"ti-helper\">Helper text</div>\n    </div>\n  `;\n  const shell = wrap.querySelector('.ti-shell');\n  const field = wrap.querySelector('.ti-field');\n  const valueRow = field.querySelector('.ti-value-row');\n  const clearBtn = field.querySelector('.ti-clear');\n  const eyeBtn = field.querySelector('.ti-eye');\n  const helper = wrap.querySelector('.ti-helper');\n  const mirror = field.querySelector('.ti-mirror');\n  const caretEl = field.querySelector('.ti-caret');\n  let dotsContainer = field.querySelector('.ti-dots');\n  let realInput = field.querySelector('.ti-input');\n  let hiddenValue = '';\n  let revealed = false;\n\n  field.classList.toggle('ti-has-leading', !!leadingSvg);\n  field.classList.toggle('ti-show-eye', tiState.password);\n  // Standard is always Caption mode — the Caption/Inline toggle only applies to Search.\n\n  mirror.style.fontFamily = 'inherit';\n  mirror.style.fontWeight = '650';\n  mirror.style.fontSize = tiState.size==='small' ? '13px' : '16px';\n  const placeCaret = tiMakeCaretDriver(valueRow, mirror, caretEl);\n\n  function currentText(){ return tiState.password ? hiddenValue : (realInput ? realInput.value : ''); }\n\n  function renderPasswordField(){\n    if(revealed){ dotsContainer.classList.add('ti-dots--text'); dotsContainer.textContent = hiddenValue; }\n    else { dotsContainer.classList.remove('ti-dots--text'); tiRenderPasswordDots(dotsContainer, hiddenValue.length); }\n  }\n\n  function reflect(focused){\n    const text = currentText();\n    const hasText = text.length>0;\n    shell.classList.toggle('ti-focused', focused);\n    shell.classList.toggle('ti-floated', focused || hasText);\n    shell.classList.toggle('ti-has-value', hasText);\n    shell.classList.toggle('ti-show-clear', focused && hasText);\n    caretEl.classList.toggle('on', focused);\n    if(tiState.password && !revealed){\n      mirror.textContent='';\n      const dotsWidth = dotsContainer ? dotsContainer.getBoundingClientRect().width : 0;\n      caretEl.style.left = (dotsWidth ? dotsWidth+4 : 0) + 'px';\n    } else {\n      placeCaret(text);\n    }\n    let label='default';\n    if(focused && hasText) label='typing'; else if(focused) label='in focus'; else if(hasText) label='complete';\n    tiUpdateReadout(label);\n  }\n\n  if(tiState.password){\n    const dotsWrap = document.createElement('div');\n    dotsWrap.className='ti-dots';\n    valueRow.insertBefore(dotsWrap, valueRow.firstChild);\n    dotsContainer = dotsWrap;\n    field.tabIndex = 0;\n    field.addEventListener('focus', ()=>reflect(true));\n    field.addEventListener('blur', ()=>reflect(false));\n    field.addEventListener('keydown', (e)=>{\n      if(e.key==='Backspace'){ hiddenValue = hiddenValue.slice(0,-1); }\n      else if(e.key.length===1){ hiddenValue += e.key; }\n      renderPasswordField();\n      reflect(true);\n    });\n    eyeBtn.addEventListener('mousedown', (e)=>e.preventDefault());\n    eyeBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{\n      revealed = !revealed;\n      eyeBtn.innerHTML = revealed ? TI_EYE_HIDE_SVG : TI_EYE_SHOW_SVG;\n      eyeBtn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(revealed));\n      renderPasswordField();\n      reflect(document.activeElement===field);\n    });\n  } else {\n    realInput.addEventListener('focus', ()=>reflect(true));\n    realInput.addEventListener('blur', ()=>reflect(false));\n    realInput.addEventListener('input', ()=>reflect(true));\n  }\n\n  clearBtn.addEventListener('mousedown', (e)=>e.preventDefault());\n  clearBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{\n    hiddenValue='';\n    if(realInput) realInput.value='';\n    if(dotsContainer) dotsContainer.innerHTML='';\n    if(!tiState.password && realInput) realInput.focus();\n    reflect(!!(realInput && document.activeElement===realInput));\n  });\n\n  // Force error / show helper — driven by the sidebar toggles, applied once at build time.\n  const showError = tiState.forceError;\n  shell.classList.toggle('ti-error', showError);\n  const helperVisible = showError || tiState.showHelper;\n  helper.classList.toggle('show', helperVisible);\n  helper.classList.toggle('ti-error-text', showError);\n  helper.textContent = showError ? 'Error text' : 'Helper text';\n\n  reflect(false);\n  return { el: wrap, field: shell };\n}\n\nfunction tiBuildSearchField(){\n  const iconSvg = TI_ICONS[tiState.searchIcon][tiState.size];\n  const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n  wrap.innerHTML = `\n    <div class=\"ti-search\" data-bg=\"${tiState.bg}\" data-size=\"${tiState.size}\">\n      <div class=\"ti-search-icon\">${iconSvg}</div>\n      <div class=\"ti-search-body\">\n        <span class=\"ti-search-label\">Label</span>\n        <div class=\"ti-search-value-row\">\n          <input class=\"ti-search-input\" type=\"text\" autocomplete=\"off\" spellcheck=\"false\"/>\n          <span class=\"ti-mirror\"></span>\n          <span class=\"ti-caret\"></span>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"ti-search-trailing\">\n        <span class=\"ti-search-spinner\">${TI_SPINNER_SVG}</span>\n        <button class=\"ti-search-clear\" type=\"button\" aria-label=\"Clear\">${TI_CLEAR_SVG}</button>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n  `;\n  const field = wrap.querySelector('.ti-search');\n  const valueRow = field.querySelector('.ti-search-value-row');\n  const input = wrap.querySelector('.ti-search-input');\n  const clearBtn = wrap.querySelector('.ti-search-clear');\n  const mirror = field.querySelector('.ti-mirror');\n  const caretEl = field.querySelector('.ti-caret');\n  mirror.style.fontFamily = 'inherit';\n  mirror.style.fontWeight = '650';\n  mirror.style.fontSize = tiState.size==='small' ? '13px' : '16px';\n  const placeCaret = tiMakeCaretDriver(valueRow, mirror, caretEl);\n\n  field.classList.toggle('ti-inline', tiState.labelMode==='inline');\n  field.classList.toggle('ti-loading', tiState.loading);\n\n  // Loading only ever shows against a real query — turns on when the user\n  // submits (Enter) with text present, and off the instant the field is empty.\n  function setLoading(on){\n    tiState.loading = on;\n    field.classList.toggle('ti-loading', on);\n    const toggle = document.getElementById('ti-toggle-loading');\n    if(toggle) toggle.classList.toggle('on', on);\n  }\n\n  function reflect(focused, opts){\n    const hasText = input.value.length>0;\n    field.classList.toggle('ti-focused', focused);\n    field.classList.toggle('ti-floated', focused || hasText);\n    field.classList.toggle('ti-has-value', hasText);\n    field.classList.toggle('ti-show-clear', focused && hasText);\n    caretEl.classList.toggle('on', focused);\n    placeCaret(input.value);\n    if(!hasText && tiState.loading && !(opts && opts.initial)) setLoading(false);\n    let label='default';\n    if(focused && hasText) label='typing'; else if(focused) label='in focus'; else if(hasText) label='complete';\n    tiUpdateReadout(label);\n  }\n  input.addEventListener('focus', ()=>reflect(true));\n  input.addEventListener('blur', ()=>reflect(false));\n  input.addEventListener('input', ()=>reflect(true));\n  input.addEventListener('keydown', (e)=>{ if(e.key==='Enter' && input.value.length>0){ setLoading(true); } });\n  clearBtn.addEventListener('mousedown', e=>e.preventDefault());\n  clearBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{ input.value=''; input.focus(); reflect(true); });\n\n  field.classList.toggle('ti-error', tiState.forceError);\n\n  reflect(false, {initial:true});\n  return { el: wrap, field };\n}",
  "usage": {
    "do": [
      "Use the Standard field for any value the user types and submits — names, amounts, references, passwords.",
      "Default to Caption label mode (the label floats above the value) so the field’s purpose stays visible once it’s filled in; reach for Inline only in tight, compact layouts where a persistent floated label would crowd the row.",
      "Use the Search pill only for filtering/finding within a results set, and pair it with a real loading state while results are being fetched.",
      "Show helper text for format guidance (e.g. expected pattern) and switch to the error state with a concrete, specific message when validation actually fails."
    ],
    "dont": [
      "Don’t use the Search pill as a general-purpose text field — its shape and icon promise filtering, not data entry.",
      "Don’t rely on placeholder text as the only label — every field keeps a real, persistent label so the value’s meaning is never lost once it’s filled in.",
      "Don’t show the error state without a specific, actionable message — a red border with no explanation just tells the user something’s wrong, not what to fix.",
      "Don’t add a leading or trailing icon purely for decoration — every icon slot should communicate something (an action, a field type, a state)."
    ]
  },

  "note": "Covers the Standard (floating/inline label) and Search (pill) field families. TI_ICONS (the icon SVG set) is intentionally excluded — it's 50KB+ of decorative markup, not structural — see the live source directly for icon glyphs if needed."
}

Checkboxes & Radios v1.1.1

Selection controls built on real native inputs, styled with the brand green. 2 control types · 3 sizes · 5 states · light & dark mode. Checkboxes for independent on/off choices; radios for one-of-many.

Quick copy
Grab a ready-made instance. Every control here is a real, focusable native input.
Quick copy
Use these instances if you’re here to quickly grab a copy.
Labels & tap target
Always wrap the control and its text in a single <label> so the whole row is clickable. Keep the interactive row at least 44×44px for comfortable touch targets.
When to use which
Checkboxes and radios look similar but answer different questions.
✓ Do
  • Use a checkbox for independent on/off options, or a single opt-in (terms, marketing).
  • Use radios when exactly one option from a set must be chosen and all options are worth showing.
  • Give every control a visible, clickable text label.
  • Pre-select a sensible default for radio groups.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use radios for a yes/no toggle — use a single checkbox or a switch.
  • Don’t use checkboxes when only one choice is allowed.
  • Don’t leave a radio group with no option selected once the user has interacted.
  • Don’t nest more than one level of dependent checkboxes.

Tags & Badges v1.1.2

Static labelling: tags for categorising, count badges for notifications, avatar badges for identity, and status dots for state · 5 tag variants · light & dark mode · interactive tag playground.

Tag or Chip?
Both are small pills of text — the difference is emphasis and interactivity. Reach for a tag to quietly categorise; reach for a Chip when the element is selectable, removable, or needs to shout.
✓ Do
  • Use a tag for read-only metadata — a transaction type, an API version, a category like “Betting”.
  • Use a count badge for unread or pending totals, and its dot-only form when the exact number doesn’t matter.
  • Use a status dot inline with a label to show live state — Active, Degraded, Offline.
  • Keep tag colour meaningful — lean on Neutral unless a semantic colour genuinely adds signal.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t make a tag clickable or removable — that’s a chip’s job.
  • Don’t stack more than a couple of tags on one row — they stop reading as metadata and start looking like filters.
  • Don’t show a count badge with “0” — hide it, or drop to a dot.
  • Don’t rely on dot colour alone for critical status — pair it with a text label.

Do's & don'ts
A few simple rules that keep chips readable and predictable.
✓ Do
  • Keep labels to a word or two so they stay easy to scan.
  • Match the colour to the meaning — green for done, red for a problem.
  • Group related chips together, like a row of filters.

Components

Cards v1.0.1

A surface that groups related content and actions into a single unit. Composed from an optional media band, a body (title, description, content) and an optional footer for actions. Built on Flash surface and border tokens, so it adapts to light & dark.

Anatomy
A basic card is a body with a title and description. Add a footer for actions, and a media band for imagery — use only what each card needs.
Basic card
Just a body with a title and a short description. The simplest, most common shape.
With footer
A footer separates primary and secondary actions from the content above.
Media & interactive
A media band sits flush at the top. An interactive card lifts on hover and makes the whole surface a single target — use it when the entire card links somewhere.
Media card
An image or thumbnail band above the body, useful for products, articles and previews.
Interactive card →
Hover me. The whole card is one clickable target with a subtle lift and shadow.
Specs
Shared measurements and the tokens behind the surface.
PropertyValueToken
Corner radius14px—
Border1pxchrome-border
SurfaceBase backgroundchrome-bg
Body padding18pxspacing-225
Footer actionPrimary (black) button
When to use
A card groups one coherent thing. If content isn’t related, don’t box it together.
✓ Do
  • Group a single, self-contained subject — one product, one summary, one record.
  • Keep one clear primary action per card, in the footer.
  • Make the whole card clickable only when it links to one destination.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t cram unrelated content into one card to save space.
  • Don’t nest cards inside cards — flatten the hierarchy.
  • Don’t put several competing primary actions in one footer.

Components

Bottom Sheets v1.0.2

A drawer-style sheet that slides up from the bottom of the screen, built from the SheetHeader block (with or without a back arrow, compact or full screen) plus a body and a footer button group. Flash brand only · interactive playground included.

When to use which
Bottom sheets and dialogs both interrupt the current screen to ask for input or show detail — the right choice depends on how much room the content needs and how attached it is to the page underneath.
✓ Do
  • Use a compact sheet for a short, focused task — confirming an action, picking from a short list, showing a summary.
  • Use full screen when the content needs the whole viewport — a multi-field form, a long list, or a flow with its own steps.
  • Add the back arrow only when the sheet is one step in a flow the person can step back out of.
  • Keep the footer to one primary action, with a secondary action alongside it where needed.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a bottom sheet for a simple yes/no confirmation — a dialog is quicker to dismiss and keeps context visible.
  • Don’t add a back arrow on the first step of a flow — there’s nowhere for it to go.
  • Don’t drop the drag handle on a full screen sheet — it’s still dismissible by swipe, so the affordance should stay.
  • Don’t bury the primary action below the fold on a full screen sheet — keep the footer pinned.

Navigation v1.1.2

The primary Side Nav for switching between top-level destinations. The full panel stacks four regions — a logo, a company block with an account selector, the nav menu, and an account footer. Each Nav item pairs an icon chip with a single-line label; the active item is marked by a brand-green chip. Works in Regular or Small, across White, Charcoal and Dark green contexts.

Anatomy
Top to bottom: Logo (Flash wordmark + secondary title) · Company (icon badge, company title and an account selector) · Nav menu (icon-chip nav items) · Account (secondary links, a divider, the signed-in user and log out). The company block sits at the top and the account footer pins to the bottom.
Interactive
The complete panel. Click an item to make it active; switch the colour context and size and it re-renders live.
Colour
Size
Nav colour
Pick the context that matches the surrounding chrome. The active item’s icon chip stays brand green in every context — it’s the one consistent marker of “you are here.”
States
A nav item resolves to one of these. Inactive is a grey chip with a subtle glyph and subtle label; Hover adds a faint row wash and lifts the label to primary; Active switches the chip to brand green with an inverse glyph and a primary label — no row fill; Focused shows the keyboard ring. Shown on White; Charcoal and Dark green follow the same logic and can be tried live above.
Anatomy & specs
Regular mirrors the Figma “Large” variant; Small mirrors the Figma “Small” variant.
PropertyRegularSmallToken
Panel width208px170px—
Panel padding20px 16px10px 10px 15px—
Corner radius12px12pxradius-small
Item padding4px 8px4px 8px · min-height 40pxradius radius-xsmall 6px
Icon chip20px glyph · 6px pad12px glyph · 4px padradius 6px
Label16px / bold12px / boldBody m / Body xs — single line
Idle chip / glyph / label#DDD chip · #A4A4A4 glyph · #8A8A8A labelgrey-400 / grey-700 / grey-800
Active markerBrand-green chip, inverse glyph, primary label — no row fillicon-secondary #10C504
When to use
Side Nav is for primary, top-level destinations that persist across a session — not for switching views within one screen.
✓ Do
  • Reserve it for a handful of top-level, persistent destinations.
  • Keep exactly one item active, matching the current page.
  • Pick one colour context and one size for the whole panel.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use Side Nav to switch tabs within a single page — that’s Tabs.
  • Don’t mix icon chips and plain-text items in the same list.
  • Don’t leave more than one item marked active at once.

Components

Tabs v1.2.1

A horizontal tab bar for switching between views within a single screen. Built from a Tab item (with or without a leading icon, in Regular or Small) composed into a Tabs list that shares one bottom divider. The active tab is marked by a weighted label and an inverse underline. Adapts to light & dark via semantic tokens.

Interactive
A working Tabs list — click any tab to switch the panel below. Only one tab is active at a time; the underline slides to the selected item.
Sizes
Regular (56px tall, 16px label) is the default for primary, page-level navigation. Small (46px tall, 13px label) suits denser or secondary contexts such as inside a card or panel.
With & without icon
A tab item can carry an optional leading icon in a rounded neutral chip. Use icons only when they add scanning value — keep every tab in a list consistent, either all with icons or all without.
States
Every tab item resolves to one of three states. Inactive uses tertiary text at medium weight with a muted icon glyph; Hover lifts the label and glyph to primary; Active keeps primary text at semibold, darkens the glyph and adds the underline. Shown here for both sizes, with and without the icon.
Anatomy & specs
Measurements and tokens per size. The active underline straddles the list’s 2px divider so it reads as a single continuous edge.
PropertyRegularSmallToken
Height56px46px—
Horizontal padding20px12pxspacing-250 / spacing-150
Vertical padding4px4pxspacing-050
Icon ↔ label gap8px6pxspacing-100 / spacing-075
Label size16px13pxBody m / Body s
Icon chip12px glyph · 4px pad11px glyph · 4px padbg surface-neutral-secondary #E6E6E6 · radius 6px
Icon glyph colourInactive #5F6261 → Active #000000chrome-muted → text-primary
Active underline4px tall, offset −2px3px tall, flushsurface-base-inverse #000 (dark #FFF)
When to use
Tabs switch between peer views of the same context without leaving the screen — they are not a substitute for primary navigation between destinations.
✓ Do
  • Use tabs to switch between related views of one object — Overview, Activity, Settings.
  • Keep exactly one tab active at all times, and default to the most useful view.
  • Keep labels short and parallel — ideally one or two words each.
  • Pick one size and one icon treatment for the whole list, and stay consistent.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use tabs to move between unrelated destinations — that’s navigation, not tabs.
  • Don’t mix icon and no-icon tabs, or Regular and Small, in the same list.
  • Don’t overflow with too many tabs — if it scrolls a lot, reconsider the structure.
  • Don’t leave the list with no active tab, or with more than one active at once.

Components

Dropdown v1.2.1

A labelled select trigger that opens a card of options, in single-select (one exclusive choice, a plain label with a trailing check) or multi-select (several independent checkboxes) form. Built from a Dropdown field (label, trigger button, assistive caption) in Bordered or Rounded style, Medium or Small size, paired with a Dropdown list item inside the options card, plus an optional search input.

Single-select
A working dropdown — click the trigger to open the list, click an option to select it and close. Click outside or press Esc to dismiss without changing the selection.
Multi-select
Click as many options as needed — each checkbox toggles independently and the menu stays open. The trigger summarises the pick as a label, or “N selected” once there’s more than one. Use Clear to reset, or Done to close.
Style
Bordered shows a visible grey outline at rest — use it wherever it needs to read clearly as a form field. Rounded hides the outline until hover/focus/open, for a softer, pill-shaped trigger that suits denser filter bars.
Sizes
Medium (48px trigger) is the default for standalone forms. Small (40px trigger) suits denser contexts such as filter rows or table toolbars.
Placeholder & selected
With no option chosen, the trigger shows a subtle placeholder in Body m – semibold / text-subtle. Once an option is selected, the same slot switches to text-primary and keeps the selected item highlighted in the list.
States
Every trigger resolves to one of four states. Default sits on a muted fill; Hover darkens the fill slightly; Keyboard focus and Open both switch the border to the inverse colour, and Open additionally flips the chevron and reveals the options card.
Options list & search
Each row is a Dropdown list item — hover-highlighted, with the active choice on a success tint. Single-select shows a trailing check mark; multi-select (above) shows a real checkbox, since more than one row can be active. The card can optionally lead with a search input to filter long option lists.
Anatomy & specs
Measurements and tokens per size.
PropertyMediumSmallToken

Horizontal padding12px10px—

Caption size12px mediumBody xs – medium
Default fill / border#f8f8f8 / #d1d1d1 (Bordered only)color-input-bg / color-input-border
Focus / open border#000 (dark #fff)color-input-focus
Trigger radiusBordered 6px · Rounded 999px (pill)—
Card radius / shadow12px · 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.14)—
List item selected (single)Success tint fill, trailing check markcolor-success-l / color-success-h
List item selected (multi)Success tint fill, success-coloured checkboxcolor-success-l / color-success-h
Multi-select triggerLabel when one is picked · “N selected” from two up—
Multi-select footerClear (outline) · Done (primary black)color-btn-s-bg
When to use
Dropdowns pick one value from a bounded list without leaving the current screen — they are not a substitute for navigation, and not the right tool for open-ended text entry.
✓ Do
  • Use a dropdown when there are roughly 5–15 known options.
  • Reach for multi-select only when picking several values genuinely makes sense — otherwise use single-select.
  • Always show a clear placeholder until a value is chosen — never default to a hidden first option.
  • Add the search input once a list runs past a screen’s worth of items.
  • Pair the trigger with a label and, where useful, an assistive caption explaining the choice.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a dropdown for 2–3 options — radios or a segmented control are faster to scan and select.
  • Don’t use multi-select when only one answer is ever valid — that’s just extra clicks.
  • Don’t close a multi-select menu the instant one box is ticked — let the user finish, then confirm with Done.
  • Don’t bury a primary, frequently-changed filter three menus deep — surface it directly.
  • Don’t mix Bordered and Rounded styles within the same form.
  • Don’t rely on the placeholder colour alone to signal “required” — pair it with real validation.

' dpd-field--sm' : '');\n    var label = '<div class=\"dpd-label\">' + (opts.label || 'Dropdown label') + '</div>';\n    var caption = '<div class=\"dpd-caption\">' + (opts.caption || 'Assistive caption') + '</div>';\n    var menu = menuHtml(opts.options, null, {showSearch: opts.showSearch, inline: false});\n    return '<div class=\"' + cls + '\">' + label +\n      '<div class=\"dpd-wrap\">' + triggerHtml({options: opts.options, placeholder: opts.placeholder}) + menu + '</div>' +\n      caption +\n    '</div>';\n  }\n\nfunction wireInteractive(root){\n    var wrap = root.querySelector('.dpd-wrap');\n    var trigger = wrap.querySelector('.dpd-trigger');\n    var menu = wrap.querySelector('.dpd-menu');\n    var textEl = trigger.querySelector('.dpd-trigger__text');\n    function close(){\n      wrap.classList.remove('is-open');\n      trigger.classList.remove('dpd-trigger--open');\n      menu.setAttribute('hidden', '');\n    }\n    function openMenu(){\n      wrap.classList.add('is-open');\n      trigger.classList.add('dpd-trigger--open');\n      menu.removeAttribute('hidden');\n      var search = menu.querySelector('input');\n      if(search) search.focus();\n    }\n    trigger.addEventListener('click', function(e){\n      e.stopPropagation();\n      if(wrap.classList.contains('is-open')) close(); else openMenu();\n    });\n    menu.querySelectorAll('.dpd-item').forEach(function(btn){\n      btn.addEventListener('click', function(e){\n        e.stopPropagation();\n        menu.querySelectorAll('.dpd-item').forEach(function(b){ b.classList.remove('is-selected'); });\n        btn.classList.add('is-selected');\n        textEl.textContent = btn.querySelector('.dpd-item__label').textContent;\n        trigger.classList.add('has-value');\n        close();\n      });\n    });\n    var search = menu.querySelector('input');\n    if(search){\n      search.addEventListener('click', function(e){ e.stopPropagation(); });\n      search.addEventListener('input', function(){\n        var q = search.value.trim().toLowerCase();\n        menu.querySelectorAll('.dpd-item').forEach(function(btn){\n          var txt = btn.querySelector('.dpd-item__label').textContent.toLowerCase();\n          btn.style.display = txt.indexOf(q) > -1 ? '' : 'none';\n        });\n      });\n    }\n    document.addEventListener('click', function(e){\n      if(!wrap.contains(e.target)) close();\n    });\n    document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){\n      if(e.key === 'Escape' && wrap.classList.contains('is-open')) close();\n    });\n  }\n\nfunction interactiveMultiFieldHtml(opts){\n    var cls = 'dpd-field' + (opts.style === 'rounded' ? ' dpd-field--rounded' : '') + (opts.size === 'sm' ? ' dpd-field--sm' : '');\n    var label = '<div class=\"dpd-label\">' + (opts.label || 'Dropdown label') + '</div>';\n    var caption = '<div class=\"dpd-caption\">' + (opts.caption || 'Assistive caption') + '</div>';\n    var items = opts.options.map(function(o){ return itemHtmlCheckbox(o, false); }).join('');\n    var search = opts.showSearch ? ('<div class=\"dpd-search\">' + SEARCH_ICON + '<input type=\"text\" placeholder=\"Search\" aria-label=\"Search options\"></div>') : '';\n    var foot = '<div class=\"dpd-menu__foot\"><button type=\"button\" class=\"dpd-menu__clear\">Clear</button><button type=\"button\" class=\"pop__apply\">Done</button></div>';\n    var menu = '<div class=\"dpd-menu\" hidden>' + search + items + foot + '</div>';\n    return '<div class=\"' + cls + '\">' + label +\n      '<div class=\"dpd-wrap\">' + triggerHtml({options: opts.options, placeholder: opts.placeholder}) + menu + '</div>' +\n      caption +\n    '</div>';\n  }\n\nfunction wireInteractiveMulti(root, opts){\n    var wrap = root.querySelector('.dpd-wrap');\n    var trigger = wrap.querySelector('.dpd-trigger');\n    var menu = wrap.querySelector('.dpd-menu');\n    var textEl = trigger.querySelector('.dpd-trigger__text');\n    var options = opts.options;\n    var selected = new Set();\n    function close(){\n      wrap.classList.remove('is-open');\n      trigger.classList.remove('dpd-trigger--open');\n      menu.setAttribute('hidden', '');\n    }\n    function openMenu(){\n      wrap.classList.add('is-open');\n      trigger.classList.add('dpd-trigger--open');\n      menu.removeAttribute('hidden');\n      var search = menu.querySelector('input');\n      if(search) search.focus();\n    }\n    function updateTrigger(){\n      if(selected.size === 0){\n        textEl.textContent = opts.placeholder || 'Choose an option';\n        trigger.classList.remove('has-value');\n      } else if(selected.size === 1){\n        textEl.textContent = options[selected.values().next().value];\n        trigger.classList.add('has-value');\n      } else {\n        textEl.textContent = selected.size + ' selected';\n        trigger.classList.add('has-value');\n      }\n    }\n    trigger.addEventListener('click', function(e){\n      e.stopPropagation();\n      if(wrap.classList.contains('is-open')) close(); else openMenu();\n    });\n    var itemEls = Array.prototype.slice.call(menu.querySelectorAll('.dpd-item'));\n    itemEls.forEach(function(btn, i){\n      btn.addEventListener('click', function(e){\n        e.stopPropagation();\n        if(selected.has(i)){ selected.delete(i); btn.classList.remove('is-selected'); }\n        else { selected.add(i); btn.classList.add('is-selected'); }\n        updateTrigger();\n      });\n    });\n    var clearBtn = menu.querySelector('.dpd-menu__clear');\n    if(clearBtn) clearBtn.addEventListener('click', function(e){\n      e.stopPropagation();\n      selected.clear();\n      itemEls.forEach(function(b){ b.classList.remove('is-selected'); });\n      updateTrigger();\n    });\n    var doneBtn = menu.querySelector('.pop__apply');\n    if(doneBtn) doneBtn.addEventListener('click', function(e){ e.stopPropagation(); close(); });\n    var search = menu.querySelector('.dpd-search input');\n    if(search){\n      search.addEventListener('click', function(e){ e.stopPropagation(); });\n      search.addEventListener('input', function(){\n        var q = search.value.trim().toLowerCase();\n        itemEls.forEach(function(btn){\n          var txt = btn.querySelector('.dpd-item__label').textContent.toLowerCase();\n          btn.style.display = txt.indexOf(q) > -1 ? '' : 'none';\n        });\n      });\n    }\n    document.addEventListener('click', function(e){\n      if(!wrap.contains(e.target)) close();\n    });\n    document.addEventListener('keydown', function(e){\n      if(e.key === 'Escape' && wrap.classList.contains('is-open')) close();\n    });\n    updateTrigger();\n  }\n\nvar CHEVRON = '<svg viewBox=\"0 0 12 8\" fill=\"none\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\"><path d=\"M1 1.5L6 6.5L11 1.5\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.6\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"/></svg>';\n\nvar SEARCH_ICON = '<svg viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" fill=\"none\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\"><circle cx=\"7\" cy=\"7\" r=\"5\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.6\"/><path d=\"M11.5 11.5L15 15\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.6\" stroke-linecap=\"round\"/></svg>';\n\nvar CHECK_ICON = '<svg viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" fill=\"none\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\"><path d=\"M3 8.5L6.5 12L13 4.5\" stroke=\"currentColor\" stroke-width=\"1.8\" stroke-linecap=\"round\" stroke-linejoin=\"round\"/></svg>';\n\nvar OPTIONS = ['Airtime & Data','Electricity','Bill Payments','Vouchers','Gaming','Insurance','Lottery','Data Bundles'];",
  "usage": {
    "do": [
      "Use a dropdown when there are roughly 5–15 known options.",
      "Reach for multi-select only when picking several values genuinely makes sense — otherwise use single-select.",
      "Always show a clear placeholder until a value is chosen — never default to a hidden first option.",
      "Add the search input once a list runs past a screen’s worth of items.",
      "Pair the trigger with a label and, where useful, an assistive caption explaining the choice."
    ],
    "dont": [
      "Don’t use a dropdown for 2–3 options — radios or a segmented control are faster to scan and select.",
      "Don’t use multi-select when only one answer is ever valid — that’s just extra clicks.",
      "Don’t close a multi-select menu the instant one box is ticked — let the user finish, then confirm with Done.",
      "Don’t bury a primary, frequently-changed filter three menus deep — surface it directly.",
      "Don’t mix Bordered and Rounded styles within the same form.",
      "Don’t rely on the placeholder colour alone to signal “required” — pair it with real validation."
    ]
  },

}

Patterns for surfacing numbers and records — stat tiles, tables, key–value lists, progress meters and filter chips. All built on chrome and semantic tokens, so they adapt to light & dark automatically.

Components

Tables v1.1.3

A selectable, row-based Table Row for records and transactions. Each row is assembled from cells — the List building block — starting with a leading checkbox, a product icon and a bold primary label, then any number of data cells, a status tag and optional trailing links. Rows resolve to five states and stack under a select-all header to form a full table. Adapts to light & dark via semantic tokens.

Playground
Customise a single Table Row live — swap the product and status, preview any of the five states, or click the checkbox to select it. Trailing links are revealed on hover, so they appear in the Hover state.
Interactive table
A working transactions table — tick any row to select it (the row tints green), or use the header checkbox to select or clear every row at once. Hover a row (or tab to it) to reveal its trailing link actions.

States
Every table row resolves to one of five states. Default sits on the base surface; Hover fills with a subtle neutral; Focused draws a 2px inverse outline for keyboard navigation; Checked tints the row and fills the checkbox in brand green; Disabled greys the content and blocks interaction.

The cell (List building block)
Rows are composed from a small set of interchangeable cells. Mix and match them to fit the data — a row needs only the leading checkbox and one labelled cell to be valid.
CellPurposeNotes
CheckboxRow selectionAlways leads the row; drives the Checked state and the header select-all.
Product iconVisual identifier30px rounded tile · radius 7px. 1Voucher orange #FF5F00, Gift Voucher pink #E43E79.
NamePrimary labelBody m semibold · 16px, text-primary. One per row.
TextData valueBody m medium. Repeatable — add one per column.
TagStatusPending (neutral), Success (green), Failed (red).
LinkRow actionOptional trailing links; pinned to the right edge.

When to use
Tables are for scannable, comparable records where rows can be selected and acted on — not for free-form content or a handful of key–value facts.
✓ Do
  • Use a table for lists of like records — transactions, stores, tickets — that users scan and compare.
  • Lead every row with the checkbox when rows can be selected, and pair it with a header select-all.
  • Right-align amounts and other numerics, and keep them tabular so digits line up.
  • Use the status tag sparingly — one per row — and keep its colour meaning consistent.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t reach for a table to show a few facts about one object — use a key–value list.
  • Don’t stack more than a couple of trailing links per row — move overflow into a menu.
  • Don’t leave a disabled row interactive — grey it and block selection.
  • Don’t mix left- and right-alignment for the same column across rows.

Do's & don'ts
A switch applies its setting immediately, with no confirmation step. Use a checkbox when a change should wait for a Save action.
✓ Do
  • Use for a single setting that takes effect the moment it’s toggled.
  • Pair every switch with a clear text label describing the “on” state.
  • Keep the label static — don’t change its wording between on and off.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a switch inside a form that needs a Save button — use a checkbox.
  • Don’t use switches for multi-select lists — that’s checkboxes.
  • Don’t rely on colour alone; the thumb position must read clearly too.

Tooltip v1.0.1

A small floating label that explains an element on hover or keyboard focus. Pure CSS — it appears on :hover and :focus-within, so keyboard users get it too. Reserve it for short, non-essential hints.

Placements
Hover or tab to each trigger. The bubble uses the inverse surface so it reads as an overlay in both light and dark. Four placements cover most anchoring needs.
Appears above Appears right Appears below Appears left
On an icon button
The most common use: naming an icon-only control so its purpose is never a guess.
Copy to clipboard More information Delete row
When to use
Tooltips are supplementary. If the user must read it to succeed, put it on the page instead.
✓ Do
  • Label icon-only buttons and clarify terse controls.
  • Keep the text to a short phrase — a line or two at most.
  • Make triggers focusable so keyboard users can reveal them.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t hide essential information or actions inside a tooltip.
  • Don’t put links, buttons or long copy in one — use a popover.
  • Don’t depend on hover alone on touch devices, where it never fires.

Accordion v1.0.1

Stacked headers that expand to reveal content, for progressively disclosing long or secondary information. Built on native <details> elements, so expand/collapse works without JavaScript and stays accessible.

Single open
Grouped with a shared name, so opening one item closes the others — ideal for FAQs where one answer at a time keeps things tidy.
How do payouts work?›
Settled funds are paid to your linked account on the next business day. You can review every payout and its breakdown in the Payouts tab.
Can I refund a transaction?›
Yes — full or partial refunds can be issued from a transaction’s detail view for up to 180 days after the sale.
Which cards are supported?›
All major schemes are accepted, including Visa, Mastercard and domestic debit networks.
Multiple open
Without a shared name, items open independently, so several can be expanded at once. Use this when sections are unrelated.
Business details›
Legal entity name, registration number and trading address.
Bank account›
The account where settled funds are deposited.
When to use
Accordions trade visibility for density. Only fold away content the user won’t always need.
✓ Do
  • Use for FAQs, optional settings and long secondary content.
  • Write headers that describe exactly what’s inside.
  • Default the most useful item open when it helps.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t bury content users need on every visit.
  • Don’t nest accordions inside accordions.
  • Don’t use one for a single item — just show it.

Alert v1.1.1

An inline banner that draws attention to a status or message tied to the surrounding content. Four semantic variants map straight onto the Flash Info / Success / Warning / Critical tokens, so they stay on-brand in light and dark.

Variants
Each variant carries a matching tinted background and icon. Keep the title to a few words and the message to a sentence or two.
i
Heads up
Your monthly statement for June is now available to download.
✓
Payment received
R1,250.00 has been settled to your account.
!
Verify your account
Add your bank details before your first payout to avoid delays.
×
Transaction failed
The card was declined. Ask the customer to try another method.
Dismissible
Add a close affordance for messages the user can clear. Keep persistent, action-critical alerts non-dismissible.
i
New feature
You can now export transactions to CSV from the Reports page.
When to use
Alerts belong in the page, next to what they describe. For transient confirmations use a toast; for blocking decisions use a dialog.
✓ Do
  • Place the alert next to the content or form it refers to.
  • Match the variant to the severity of the message.
  • Lead with a short title, then a plain-language explanation.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use an alert for a fleeting confirmation — that’s a toast.
  • Don’t stack many alerts — prioritise the one that matters.
  • Don’t use critical red for routine, non-urgent information.

Skeleton loader v1.0.2

A shimmering placeholder that mirrors content’s shape while it loads, so the layout doesn’t jump when data arrives. Built from neutral surface tokens and honours prefers-reduced-motion.

Building blocks
Compose skeletons from three primitives — lines, blocks and circles — sized to match the real content they stand in for.
Text lines
Circle
Block
Composed
Real-world groupings: a media row (avatar + two lines) and a content card. Match the skeleton to the component it replaces.
When to use
Skeleton loaders work best when you know the shape of what’s coming and the wait is more than a moment.
✓ Do
  • Mirror the final layout so content doesn’t shift on load.
  • Use for lists, tables and cards fetched from the network.
  • Keep the shimmer subtle and stop it for reduced-motion users.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a skeleton for a sub-second load — it just flickers.
  • Don’t use one for a small indeterminate action — use a spinner.
  • Don’t let the placeholder differ wildly from the real content.

Spinner v1.1.1

An indeterminate loading indicator for short waits where progress can’t be measured. Two styles cover most needs: a solid arc spinning over a neutral ring, or a fading 8-blade activity indicator (from the Figma component library). Both flip black/white with the theme.

Type
Ring is the default — compact and works well at small sizes. Activity is a fading blade wheel, useful where a slightly richer loading motif suits the surface.
Ring
Activity
Ring sizes
Small (16px) for inline and buttons, Regular (24px) as the default, Large (36px) for full-block loading.
Small
Regular
Large
Activity sizes
The same three steps, built as an 8-blade SVG that fades around the wheel instead of a rotating arc.
Small
Regular
Large
In context
On a busy primary button the indicator switches to the button’s text colour; inline it sits beside a label. Either type works in both places — pick one per surface and stay consistent.
Processing… Loading transactions… Syncing account…
When to use
A spinner says “working” without saying how long. For content whose shape you know, a skeleton feels faster.
✓ Do
  • Use for short, indeterminate waits — submitting, saving, fetching.
  • Place it where the result will appear, or inside the triggering button.
  • Keep one spinner per action, not many at once.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a spinner for long, content-shaped loads — use a skeleton.
  • Don’t leave it spinning with no resolution or error path.
  • Don’t scatter multiple spinners across one view.

Breadcrumb v1.0.1

A trail showing where the current page sits in the hierarchy, and a one-click route back up. Ancestors are muted links; the current page is a non-interactive, weighted label.

Standard
Each level links to its parent; a chevron separates them. The last item is the current page and isn’t a link.
Dashboard › Transactions › June 2026 › Payout #4821
Truncated
When a deep path would wrap or crowd the header, collapse the middle into an ellipsis and keep the root and the last step or two.
Dashboard › … › June 2026 › Payout #4821
When to use
Breadcrumbs orient users in deep structures. In a flat app they add clutter without value.
✓ Do
  • Use in hierarchies three or more levels deep.
  • Make every ancestor a working link; leave the current page plain.
  • Collapse the middle with an ellipsis when space is tight.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use breadcrumbs as the primary navigation.
  • Don’t add them to flat, one- or two-level structures.
  • Don’t link the current page to itself.

Pagination v1.0.1

Page-by-page navigation through a large set of results. The active page is marked with the solid primary (black) tile; long ranges collapse to an ellipsis so the control stays compact.

Interactive
Click a page or the arrows — the active page updates and the visible range recalculates around it. Prev/Next disable at the ends.
Compact
Where horizontal space is scarce — toolbars, cards, mobile — pair the arrows with a plain “Page X of Y” status.
Page 1 of 24
When to use
Pagination gives users control and a sense of scale. For continuous feeds, infinite scroll may fit better.
✓ Do
  • Use for large, countable result sets and data tables.
  • Always show the current page and keep Prev/Next reachable.
  • Collapse long ranges with an ellipsis around the active page.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t paginate a handful of items — just show them.
  • Don’t render dozens of raw page numbers with no truncation.
  • Don’t mix pagination and infinite scroll in the same list.

  "css": "/* ---- Pagination ---- */\n.pag { display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;flex-wrap:wrap }\n.pag__btn { min-width:34px;height:34px;padding:0 11px;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;border:1px solid var(--chrome-border);background:var(--chrome-bg);color:var(--chrome-txt);border-radius:8px;font-size:13px;font-weight:600;font-family:inherit;cursor:pointer;transition:background .15s,border-color .15s,color .15s }\n.pag__btn:hover:not(:disabled):not(.is-active) { background:var(--chrome-hover) }\n.pag__btn.is-active { background:var(--color-btn-s-bg);border-color:var(--color-btn-s-bg);color:var(--color-btn-s-txt);cursor:default }\n.pag__btn:disabled { opacity:.4;cursor:not-allowed }\n.pag__ellipsis { min-width:22px;text-align:center;color:var(--chrome-muted) }\n.pag__status { font-size:13px;color:var(--chrome-muted) }",
  "js": "function pageList(c,t){\n    var out=[], range=[];\n    for(var i=Math.max(2,c-1); i<=Math.min(t-1,c+1); i++) range.push(i);\n    out.push(1);\n    if(range.length && range[0] > 2) out.push('e');\n    range.forEach(function(p){ out.push(p); });\n    if(range.length && range[range.length-1] < t-1) out.push('e');\n    if(t>1) out.push(t);\n    return out;\n  }\n\nfunction render(){\n    var html = '<div class=\"pag\">';\n    html += '<button class=\"pag__btn\" type=\"button\" data-go=\"prev\"'+(cur===1?' disabled':'')+' aria-label=\"Previous page\">&lsaquo;</button>';\n    pageList(cur,total).forEach(function(p){\n      if(p==='e') html += '<span class=\"pag__ellipsis\">&hellip;</span>';\n      else html += '<button class=\"pag__btn'+(p===cur?' is-active':'')+'\" type=\"button\" data-go=\"'+p+'\"'+(p===cur?' aria-current=\"page\"':'')+'>'+p+'</button>';\n    });\n    html += '<button class=\"pag__btn\" type=\"button\" data-go=\"next\"'+(cur===total?' disabled':'')+' aria-label=\"Next page\">&rsaquo;</button>';\n    html += '</div>';\n    el.innerHTML = html;\n    Array.prototype.forEach.call(el.querySelectorAll('[data-go]'), function(b){\n      b.addEventListener('click', function(){\n        var g = b.getAttribute('data-go');\n        if(g==='prev') cur = Math.max(1, cur-1);\n        else if(g==='next') cur = Math.min(total, cur+1);\n        else cur = parseInt(g,10);\n        render();\n      });\n    });\n  }",

Toggle Group v1.0.1

A compact set of related toggles in one track. Single-select works as a segmented control (one choice at a time); multi-select works as a formatting toolbar (independent on/off toggles).

Single-select (segmented)
Exactly one option is active. The selected segment lifts onto a raised surface — good for switching a view or range.
Multi-select (toolbar)
Any number of toggles can be on at once; active ones fill with the solid primary (black) style. Use for formatting-style controls.
When to use
A toggle group keeps a small, fixed set of options in view. Past a handful, a dropdown scales better.
✓ Do
  • Use for 2–5 mutually exclusive options (single) or related toggles (multi).
  • Keep labels short and equal in weight.
  • Always keep one option selected in single-select mode.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use it to navigate between pages — that’s Tabs.
  • Don’t exceed a handful of options — use a dropdown instead.
  • Don’t allow an empty selection in single-select mode.

Avatar v1.1.1

A circular representation of a person or entity — a photo when available, initials or a generic glyph as fallbacks. Five sizes, an optional presence dot, and a stacked group for showing many at once.

Sizes
Five steps from 24px to 72px. Pick one size per context and stay consistent within a list.
XSMO
SMMO
MDMO
LGMO
XLMO
Types & presence
Photo shows a neutral placeholder illustration until a real image loads; initials or a generic fallback glyph cover the rest. An optional presence dot shows online / offline.
Photo
InitialsRB
Fallback
OnlineAK
OfflineJP
Group
Stack a few avatars to show shared ownership or attendees, capped with a “+N” count.
MO RB AK +3
When to use
Avatars identify people and entities at a glance. They’re identity, not decoration.
✓ Do
  • Always provide a fallback: initials, then a generic glyph.
  • Keep one avatar size consistent within a given list.
  • Add a presence dot only where online status is meaningful.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use avatars for decorative or generic imagery.
  • Don’t stretch non-square photos — always crop to fill.
  • Don’t rely on the presence dot’s colour alone to convey status.

Slider v1.0.1

A draggable control for choosing a value from a continuous or stepped range. Built on a native <input type="range"> — fully keyboard-operable — with a solid black fill and thumb (white in dark mode).

Continuous
Drag the thumb or use the arrow keys. The filled portion and the live value both track the current position.
Volume60%
Stepped
A step snaps the thumb to fixed increments — here, R100 — with min/max labels for scale.
Payout thresholdR500
R0R1,000
Disabled
A read-only or unavailable slider dims and stops responding to input.
Locked30%
When to use
A slider suits approximate values where the exact number matters less than the feel of more or less.
✓ Do
  • Use for imprecise ranges — volume, brightness, thresholds.
  • Always show the current value alongside the track.
  • Use step when only certain increments are valid.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a slider for precise numeric entry — use an input.
  • Don’t use one over a huge range where a pixel equals a big jump.
  • Don’t hide the selected value from the user.

Popover v1.0.1

A small floating panel anchored to a trigger, holding secondary content or controls. Opens on click and dismisses on outside-click or Escape — richer than a tooltip, lighter than a dialog.

Interactive
Click a trigger to open its panel; click outside or press Escape to close. Panels can carry real, interactive controls.
Filter transactions
Show refunds
Only over R100
About settlements
Funds settle to your linked account on the next business day after a sale clears.
When to use
A popover is for optional, on-demand content anchored to a control — not for essential steps or fleeting hints.
✓ Do
  • Use for contextual actions or details tied to a trigger.
  • Support outside-click and Escape to dismiss.
  • Keep the content compact and focused on one task.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a popover for a required, blocking flow — use a dialog.
  • Don’t use one for a plain text hint — use a tooltip.
  • Don’t pack a whole form or page into it.

Input OTP v1.0.1

A segmented field for one-time passcodes — SMS, email or authenticator 2FA. Each digit gets its own box; typing auto-advances, Backspace steps back, and a pasted code fills every box at once.

Six digit
The default for most verification codes. Type a digit to advance; try pasting a 6-digit number into the first box.
Four digit, grouped
A shorter PIN, split into two pairs with a separator for readability.
–
Error
On an invalid or expired code, mark the whole group and explain what to do next below it.
That code isn’t right — check it and try again.
When to use
Use an OTP field for short, fixed-length codes the user transcribes once — not for regular data entry.
✓ Do
  • Use for SMS / email verification and 2FA codes.
  • Support paste and auto-advance so entry is effortless.
  • Use inputmode="numeric" to bring up the number pad on mobile.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use segmented boxes for ordinary or variable-length input.
  • Don’t use it for long secrets or passwords — use a password field.
  • Don’t block pasting — it’s how most people enter codes.

Charts v1.0.2

Lightweight, interactive data visualisations rendered as inline SVG — no charting library. Four core types cover most needs. Hover any bar, point or segment for its value; the donut pops the hovered slice and shows its share in the centre. Series and categories use the Flash colour palette (brand green, blue, purple, orange); single-series charts lead with the brand green.

Bar
Compare discrete values across categories. Hover a bar to emphasise it and read its value; the rest dim back.
Monthly volume
Transactions per month · 2026
Line & area
Show a trend over a continuous range. The area variant fills beneath the line to emphasise volume.
Active users
Line · last 7 weeks
Settled value
Area · last 7 weeks
Donut
Show parts of a whole. Each slice takes a colour from the Flash palette; hover a slice or its legend entry to pop it out and read its share in the centre.
Payment mix
Share of volume by method
When to use
Pick the type that matches the question: comparison (bar), trend (line/area) or composition (donut).
✓ Do
  • Use bars for comparison, lines for trends, donuts for a few parts of a whole.
  • Label axes; give each category or series its own palette colour, and keep single-series charts to one.
  • Start bar and area value axes at zero.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a donut for more than ~5 segments — a bar reads better.
  • Don’t colour series just for decoration — it implies meaning that isn’t there.
  • Don’t truncate a value axis in a way that exaggerates differences.

t.innerHTML=html; t.style.left=(r.left-cr.left+r.width/2)+'px'; t.style.top=(r.top-cr.top-8)+'px'; t.classList.add('show'); }\n\nfunction lineChart(el, data, filled){\n    var card=el.closest('.cht'), tip=mkTip(card);\n    var W=340,H=168,padT=12,padB=22,padX=10, cw=W-padX*2, ch=H-padT-padB;\n    var max=Math.max.apply(null,data.map(function(d){return d.v;})), n=data.length;\n    var xs=function(i){return padX+(n<=1?0:i/(n-1)*cw);}, ys=function(v){return padT+ch-(max?v/max*ch:0);};\n    var defs='', area='';\n    if(filled){\n      defs='<defs><linearGradient id=\"chtAreaGrad\" x1=\"0\" y1=\"0\" x2=\"0\" y2=\"1\"><stop offset=\"0\" stop-color=\"var(--c1)\" stop-opacity=\"0.32\"/><stop offset=\"1\" stop-color=\"var(--c1)\" stop-opacity=\"0\"/></linearGradient></defs>';\n      var d='M '+xs(0).toFixed(1)+','+(padT+ch).toFixed(1);\n      data.forEach(function(dd,i){ d+=' L '+xs(i).toFixed(1)+','+ys(dd.v).toFixed(1); });\n      d+=' L '+xs(n-1).toFixed(1)+','+(padT+ch).toFixed(1)+' Z'; area='<path class=\"cht__area\" d=\"'+d+'\"/>';\n    }\n    var pts=data.map(function(dd,i){return xs(i).toFixed(1)+','+ys(dd.v).toFixed(1);}).join(' ');\n    var dots=data.map(function(dd,i){return '<circle class=\"cht__dot\" data-i=\"'+i+'\" cx=\"'+xs(i).toFixed(1)+'\" cy=\"'+ys(dd.v).toFixed(1)+'\" r=\"3.5\"/>';}).join('');\n    var hits=data.map(function(dd,i){ var x0=i===0?0:(xs(i-1)+xs(i))/2, x1=i===n-1?W:(xs(i)+xs(i+1))/2;\n      return '<rect class=\"cht__hit\" data-i=\"'+i+'\" x=\"'+x0.toFixed(1)+'\" y=\"0\" width=\"'+(x1-x0).toFixed(1)+'\" height=\"'+(padT+ch).toFixed(1)+'\"/>'; }).join('');\n    var labs=data.map(function(dd,i){return '<text class=\"cht__axis\" x=\"'+xs(i).toFixed(1)+'\" y=\"'+(H-7)+'\" text-anchor=\"middle\">'+dd.label+'</text>';}).join('');\n    el.innerHTML='<svg viewBox=\"0 0 '+W+' '+H+'\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Line chart\">'+defs+area+'<polyline class=\"cht__line\" points=\"'+pts+'\"/>'+dots+labs+hits+'</svg>';\n    var dotEls=el.querySelectorAll('.cht__dot');\n    Array.prototype.forEach.call(el.querySelectorAll('.cht__hit'),function(h){ var i=+h.getAttribute('data-i'), dot=dotEls[i];\n      h.addEventListener('mouseenter',function(){ dot.classList.add('on'); dot.setAttribute('r','5.5'); moveTip(tip,card,dot,'<b>'+data[i].v+'</b> &middot; '+data[i].label); });\n      h.addEventListener('mouseleave',function(){ dot.classList.remove('on'); dot.setAttribute('r','3.5'); tip.classList.remove('show'); });\n    });\n  }",
  "usage": {
    "do": [
      "Use bars for comparison, lines for trends, donuts for a few parts of a whole.",
      "Label axes; give each category or series its own palette colour, and keep single-series charts to one.",
      "Start bar and area value axes at zero."
    ],
    "dont": [
      "Don’t use a donut for more than ~5 segments — a bar reads better.",
      "Don’t colour series just for decoration — it implies meaning that isn’t there.",
      "Don’t truncate a value axis in a way that exaggerates differences."
    ]
  },

  "note": "fmt/mkTip/moveTip/lineChart are the only named builder functions; the Bar and Donut renderers are inline logic directly inside the same anonymous IIFE (keyed off document.getElementById('cht-bar')/('cht-donut') guards) rather than separately named functions, so they aren't individually extractable by identifier — reconstruct them from this file's live JS if reskinning bar/donut specifically. All series colours ride --c1..--c5 (Flash palette), not hardcoded hex."
}

Calendar & Date Picker v1.0.1

A month-grid calendar for choosing a date, and a compact field that opens it in a popover. Fully interactive — navigate months and pick a day. The selected day uses the primary (black) style; today is outlined.

Inline calendar
Use the arrows to change month; click a day to select it. Good when the calendar is always on screen — booking flows, filters.
Date picker field
A field that shows the chosen date and opens the calendar on click. Picking a day fills the field and closes the popover; click outside or press Escape to dismiss.
When to use
Pick the form that fits the space: an inline calendar when it’s central, a field when date is one input among many.
✓ Do
  • Use the field in forms; use the inline calendar when picking a date is the main task.
  • Mark today and make the selected date unmistakable.
  • Also accept typed dates for accessibility and speed where you can.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t use a calendar for far-off dates like birth year — a select is faster.
  • Don’t trap keyboard users — allow Escape and typed entry.
  • Don’t hide which month is shown or which day is selected.

Command v1.0.1

A searchable command palette for jumping to actions and destinations fast. Type to filter; use ↑ ↓ to move and Enter to run. Typically summoned with a shortcut like ⌘+K.

Interactive
Start typing to filter across groups. The highlighted row follows your arrow keys; Enter would run it.
When to use
A command palette rewards frequent, keyboard-driven users. It complements visible navigation — it doesn’t replace it.
✓ Do
  • Aggregate common actions and destinations behind one search.
  • Support full keyboard use and show shortcuts inline.
  • Group results and show a clear empty state.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t make it the only way to reach a feature.
  • Don’t dump every action in with no grouping or ranking.
  • Don’t hide it with no discoverable shortcut or entry point.

  "js": "var CMD=[\n    {group:'Navigation', items:[{ico:'⌂',label:'Go to Dashboard',kbd:'G D'},{ico:'⇄',label:'Go to Transactions',kbd:'G T'},{ico:'↑',label:'Go to Payouts'}]},\n    {group:'Actions', items:[{ico:'＋',label:'New payment link',kbd:'N'},{ico:'↓',label:'Export to CSV'},{ico:'⟳',label:'Refresh data',kbd:'R'}]},\n    {group:'Settings', items:[{ico:'☾',label:'Toggle dark mode'},{ico:'⚙',label:'Open settings',kbd:','}]}\n  ];\n\nfunction draw(){\n    var q=input.value.toLowerCase().trim(), html='', count=0;\n    CMD.forEach(function(g){\n      var m=g.items.filter(function(it){return it.label.toLowerCase().indexOf(q)>=0;});\n      if(!m.length) return;\n      html+='<div class=\"cmd__glabel\">'+g.group+'</div>';\n      m.forEach(function(it){ html+='<div class=\"cmd__item\" data-i=\"'+(count++)+'\"><span class=\"cmd__ico\">'+it.ico+'</span>'+it.label+(it.kbd?'<span class=\"kbd\">'+it.kbd+'</span>':'')+'</div>'; });\n    });\n    listEl.innerHTML=count?html:'<div class=\"cmd__empty\">No results found</div>';\n    items=Array.prototype.slice.call(listEl.querySelectorAll('.cmd__item'));\n    active=count?0:-1; hi();\n    items.forEach(function(el){ el.addEventListener('mousemove',function(){ active=+el.getAttribute('data-i'); hi(); }); });\n  }\n\nfunction hi(){ items.forEach(function(el,i){ el.classList.toggle('is-active', i===active); }); if(active>=0&&items[active]) items[active].scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}); }",

Context Menu v1.0.1

A menu of actions relevant to a specific element, opened by right-click. It appears at the pointer and dismisses on outside-click, scroll or Escape.

Interactive
Right-click (or two-finger tap) inside the area below to open the menu at your pointer.
Right-click anywhere in this area
⇗Open↵
⧉Duplicate
✎RenameF2
×Delete⌦
When to use
Context menus offer power-user shortcuts. Because they’re hidden until right-click, never make them the only path to an action.
✓ Do
  • Offer actions specific to the right-clicked item.
  • Group related actions and separate destructive ones.
  • Mirror every item in a visible menu or toolbar too.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t hide essential actions only behind right-click.
  • Don’t overload it with dozens of items.
  • Don’t place a destructive action where users expect a safe one.

Hover Card v1.0.1

A rich preview that appears when a user hovers or focuses a reference — a person, entity or link — without navigating away. Like a tooltip, but for structured content rather than a one-line hint.

Interactive
Hover (or tab to) the highlighted name. The card fades in after a short delay so it doesn’t flicker on passing hovers.

Last settlement was approved by RB Rethabile Beng@rethabile · Finance ops Approves payouts and manages settlement rules. Joined March 2024 · Cape Town. earlier today.

When to use
Hover cards enrich a reference in place. They’re optional context — never the only way to see the information.
✓ Do
  • Preview a person, record or link the user is pointing at.
  • Delay the open slightly so it doesn’t flash on pass-through.
  • Keep the content scannable — a few lines, not a page.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t put essential info only in a hover card — touch users miss it.
  • Don’t use one for a plain text hint — that’s a tooltip.
  • Don’t pack interactive-heavy flows inside — use a popover or page.

Separator v1.0.1

A thin rule that divides content into groups. Horizontal by default, vertical inside a row, or with a centred label to break a flow. One hairline on the border token, so it stays quiet in both themes.

Horizontal
The default — separates stacked blocks of content.
Account
Manage your business profile and details.
Payouts
Choose where settled funds are deposited.
Vertical & labelled
A vertical rule separates inline items; a labelled separator breaks a flow with a word like “or”.
ProfileSettingsLog out
Or continue with
When to use
A separator groups; whitespace usually does the same job more quietly. Reach for a rule only when the boundary needs to be explicit.
✓ Do
  • Divide clearly distinct groups in a list or settings page.
  • Use a vertical rule between inline actions or meta items.
  • Use a labelled separator to introduce an alternative (“or”).
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t rule between every row — let spacing do the work.
  • Don’t make separators heavy or coloured; keep them hairline.
  • Don’t stack multiple rules with no content between them.

Components

Keyboard Shortcuts v1.0.2

A small key-cap for representing keyboard input — single keys or shortcut combinations. Monospaced, with a subtle bottom edge so it reads as a physical key.

Single keys
One glyph per cap. Use the platform symbols where they help.
⌘⇧⌥CtrlEsc↵⌫K
Combinations
Chain caps with a thin plus to show a chord.
⌘+K ⌘+⇧+P Ctrl+C
In context
Inline within running text, at the size of the surrounding copy.

Press ⌘+K to open the command palette, or / to jump straight to search.

When to use
Kbd shows the user which keys to press. It’s documentation, not a button — don’t make it clickable.
✓ Do
  • Show shortcuts in menus, tooltips and the command palette.
  • Use recognised symbols and keep one glyph per cap.
  • Match the key labels to the user’s platform where you can.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t style buttons as key-caps — Kbd isn’t interactive.
  • Don’t cram a whole chord into one cap — chain separate caps.
  • Don’t invent symbols; use the platform’s standard ones.

Carousel v1.0.1

A horizontally scrollable, snapping set of slides for browsing a small collection — features, images, onboarding steps. Drag/swipe, use the arrows, or jump with the dots.

Interactive
Swipe or use the arrows; the active dot elongates to show position. Slides snap into place.
Instant payouts
Tap to pay
Fraud protection
Same-day settlement
When to use
Carousels suit small, browsable sets where each slide stands alone. They hide content behind interaction, so don’t bury anything essential.
✓ Do
  • Use for a handful of equally-weighted, self-contained slides.
  • Show position with dots and offer arrows plus swipe.
  • Keep each slide understandable on its own.
✗ Don’t
  • Don’t hide critical content or primary actions in later slides.
  • Don’t auto-advance without a pause control — it fights the reader.
  • Don’t use a carousel where a simple list would show everything at once.
